question: Will this battery pack overheat in a sealed box during a one hour discharge?
headline: Hottest point reaches 74.5 C (limit 60 C) at (19, 19.3, 31.5) mm after 60 min. It passes 60 C after about 22.5 min.
confidence_reasons: passed mesh convergence, hand calculation, units and sanity

checks.name: mesh convergence
checks.summary: temperature rise at the hottest point settled: 39.5 -> 39.5 C over 2 meshes, last change 0.0%

checks.name: hand calculation
checks.summary: lumped model with convection and radiation (Biot 0.012) gives a mean of 72.2 C at the end; FEA mean is 72.8 C (1.6% of the rise)

assumptions: Li-ion cell (lumped, effective): conductivity 3 W/(m K), specific heat 950 J/(kg K), density 2500 kg/m3.
Heat is generated evenly through the part.
Convection uses a fixed film coefficient; real coefficients vary with temperature and airflow.
Surrounding air or coolant at 35 C does not heat up.
Contact resistance between parts and internal airflow are not modeled.

_figures: Temperature with the hottest point marked

fixes.title: Raise heat transfer about 2x
fixes.summary: The temperature rise scales with 1/(h A). A small fan takes h from about 5 to 25 W/(m2 K); fins or a larger case add area. Either way you need about 2x the current 5 W/(m2 K) times area.

fixes.title: Cut the power to 3.04 W
fixes.summary: Lower current or duty cycle; the rise is proportional to the heat made.

notes: Built from pack.py with size=37, length=65.
